Litware, Inc. is an electric utility that serves 2 million customers in three regions: North, Central, and South.
- Every smart meter sends a reading every 15 seconds.
- A grid control center in Denver supervises all regions. Each region has its own team of operators.
- A data science team builds anomaly detection models in Python.

**Streaming**
- Meter readings arrive in an Azure Event Hubs event hub named meter-readings that has 32 partitions.
- Each JSON event contains MeterId, SubstationId, Region, Timestamp, VoltageV, and PowerKw.

**Fabric**
- Litware has an F128 capacity and two workspaces: Litware-Ingest and Litware-DataSci.
- Litware-Ingest contains an eventhouse named EH_Grid with a KQL database named MeterDB, a table named MeterReadings, and an eventstream named ES_Meters that reads from meter-readings.
- Litware-DataSci contains a lakehouse named LH_History with a Delta table named HistoryReadings that holds 40 TB of readings from 2019 to 2025.
- Data scientists have the Contributor role in Litware-DataSci. Ana is an operations engineer with the Contributor role in Litware-Ingest.

**Identity**
- Microsoft Entra groups: grid-control@litware.com, ops-north@litware.com, ops-central@litware.com, and ops-south@litware.com.

**Planned changes**
- Detect outages in real time and notify on-call engineers.
- Score readings with the anomaly detection model as they arrive.
- Make the historical readings available to KQL analysts.

**Technical requirements**
- Readings with a null MeterId must be dropped. Valid readings must be routed to both MeterDB and a lakehouse table, without writing code.
- Each reading must be scored by the existing Python model of the data science team, and the scores must be merged into a Delta table.
- Analysts must run ad hoc time-series queries over three years of readings and get results in seconds.
- The on-call engineer must receive a Microsoft Teams message when the voltage of a substation drops below 207 V.
- Analysts must query HistoryReadings together with MeterReadings in KQL querysets. The history must not be copied into the eventhouse.
- All notebooks and Spark job definitions in Litware-DataSci, including notebooks that pipelines run, must have the Python library pvlib 0.11 without per-notebook setup. Data scientists must not change the shared library set.

**Security requirements**
- Regional operators must see only the MeterReadings rows of their region from every client, including KQL querysets, Real-Time Dashboards, and Power BI.
- Members of grid-control@litware.com must see all rows.

**Performance and monitoring requirements**
- Outage dashboard queries must never wait for EH_Grid to reactivate.
- On weekdays from 05:00 to 09:00, EH_Grid must guarantee at least 16 CUs. Outside those hours, eventhouse cost must stay as low as possible.
- Operations must analyze eventstream errors and eventhouse ingestion results of Litware-Ingest by using KQL, and keep these logs for 90 days.
- After quiet nights, the first outage dashboard queries at 05:00 take several seconds longer than later queries.
